issue.title: Update: CORS Security Cheat Sheet
issue.body:
<!--- Please complete the sections below -->

## What is missing or needs to be updated?
currently the sheet says 
>Don't treat a preflight as authorization. A preflight OPTIONS request never includes credentials ([Fetch Standard: >CORS protocol and credentials](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#cors-protocol-and-credentials)), so answer it >without requiring a session, never perform an action on it, and authorize the actual request.

However, some browsers deviate from this requirement for TLS client certificates:
- Chromium-based browsers send TLS client certificates in CORS preflight requests
- Firefox allows this behavior when the network.cors_preflight.allow_client_cert preference is enabled

The issue was also discussed in a previous pr #2946 

## How should this be resolved?
I'd replace the existing second bullet with this:

- Don't treat a preflight as authorization. According to the Fetch Standard, a preflight `OPTIONS` request must not include credentials. However, some browsers deviate from this requirement for TLS client certificates:
  - Chromium-based browsers send TLS client certificates in CORS preflight requests [Chromium issue #775438](https://crbug.com/775438)
  - Firefox allows this behavior when the `network.cors_preflight.allow_client_cert` preference is enabled [Firefox bug #1511151](https://bugzil.la/1511151)



<!-- Thank you again for your contribution -->

comments.body: I'll be happy to write it if it gets ack.

This is my sentence from #2969, and you're right that it overstates the guarantee: the Fetch definition of credentials includes TLS client certificates, and Chrome still violates the preflight rule (crbug 775438 / issue 40089326, open, P3) while Firefox gated its behaviour behind `network.cors_preflight.allow_client_cert` (bug 1511151, fixed).

I'll implement it once the issue is ACK'd, keeping your wording.
Let others' have some fun man 🥀
Thanks @MadEyE355 yes please go ahead with PR!
